name: Survey MDD
gitignoreRaw:
# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude
# Lines that start with '#' are comments.
# For a project mostly in C, the following would be a good set of
# exclude patterns (uncomment them if you want to use them):
# *.[oa]
# *~




# 7/9/2026: generic entries


# 1. Always safe

# macOS
.DS_Store
.AppleDouble
.LSOverride
._*

# Windows
Thumbs.db
ehthumbs.db
Desktop.ini

# Windows Recycle Bin
**/$RECYCLE.BIN/

# macOS Finder
**/.Spotlight-V100/
**/.Trashes/

# Temporary Office files
~$*
*.tmp
*.temp

# Swap / editor files
*.swp
*.swo
*.bak
*.old

# Vim
*.un~



# 2. Usually safe
#
# These depend a bit more on your workflow.

# Compressed archives
*.zip
*.7z
*.rar
*.gz
*.tar
*.tgz
*.bz2

# Logs
*.log

# Temporary exports
*.cache
*.dmp

# Email temp
*.eml.tmp

# 3. IDE/editor folders (if they ever appear)

**/.vscode/
**/.idea/
*.code-workspace

**/.settings/
.project
.classpath

# 4. Python

**/__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.pyo

# 5. Node.js

**/node_modules/
npm-debug.log*

# 6. R
.Rhistory
.RData
.Ruserdata

# 7. SPSS
#
# Since you've mentioned using SPSS before, I would not ignore:

*.sav
*.zsav
*.spv

# Those are probably exactly the kinds of files you want to track.
#
# 8. Office
#
# I would also not ignore:

# *.xlsx
# *.xlsm
# *.docx
# *.pptx

# Those are likely your deliverables.

# 9. PDFs

# Personally, I'd keep:

# *.pdf

# Many reports are PDFs.

# 10. Images

# I'd also keep:

# *.png
# *.jpg
# *.jpeg
# *.gif

# Unless they're generated automatically.

# One pattern I especially like
~$*

# This ignores Office lock files such as

# ~$Report.xlsx
# ~$Presentation.pptx








# 7/9/2026: new entries after alanyzing actually existing files

# Archives
*.7z
*.zip
*.gzip

# Executables
*.exe
*.dll

# Temporary
*.tmp
*.bak
*.bat~
*.un~

# Python
*.pyc
**/__pycache__/

# Office lock files
~$*

# Windows
Thumbs.db
Desktop.ini

# macOS
.DS_Store
._*

# Shortcuts
*.lnk

# Log files
*.log

# Locker files
*.lmd

# temp mdd artifacts
M*tmp_*.mdd

# Video
*.mp4







# 7/9/2026: specific files follow ups

# I would also ignore .mtd Your reasoning convinced me. Although XML is diffable, - they're generated - they're huge - they're not pleasant to review - they can become GBs I'd ignore them.
*.mtd

# .ddf You already know they're generated binary data. Ignore.
*.ddf

# Usually SQLite or some local cache. Ignore.
.db

# I'd probably ignore .parquet Usually generated datasets. They're binary. Git doesn't compare them meaningfully.
*.parquet

# .pkl Python pickle. Binary. Usually generated.
*.pkl

# .loop Never seen one in a Git repo that was worth versioning.
*.loop

# Likewise. .ivs
*.ivs

# .swf Flash movie. Ancient. Probably generated asset.
*.swf

# .thmx PowerPoint themes. Unless you actively develop themes, ignore.
*.thmx

# backups - ignore
**/_KEEP/

# could be js map files, or could belong to some different software - anyway not files we work with; I'd ignore
*.map

# could be large files with data - I should track source scripts that are used to produce data, not the generated data-files stored in csv
*.csv

# And also, I decide to exclude all in
**/Outputs/
**/dengr/
<!-- Templates/ -->
**/TemplatesPrereshell/
**/TemplatesPre2ndReshell/
**/temp ap/
**/temp ap (safe to delete)/
**/temp ap (safe to be deleted)/
**/Logs/
**/Data/Backup*/

# fonts - no reason to see in history
*.ttf
*.eot
*.woff
